title: Measure First: A Repeatable Baseline Harness
objective: Define latency and error SLIs before looking at results, then produce a three-run baseline with p50/p95/p99 and documented variance from a single-command harness.
whyThisMatters: A speedup nobody can reproduce is a story, not a measurement. Later tasks in this term — profile, cache, load test, capacity — all cite numbers from this harness. If the baseline is a single mean from one lucky run, every later claim is untrustworthy.
evidence: A committed SLI/SLO note whose commit precedes the first results file, stating a p95 or p99 latency target and an error-rate target
The harness script or program plus a README command that produces one run
Raw output from at least three runs, each recording p50, p95, p99 and error rate
A baseline note stating the three p95 values and their numeric range
A hardware and warmup note (CPU model or instance type, how many warmup iterations were discarded)
Reflection notes answering the task questions
acceptanceCriteria: The SLI/SLO file states a p95 or p99 latency target and an error-rate target, and its commit precedes the first results file.
One documented command produces a run that prints or writes p50, p95 and p99 — not only a mean.
At least three run output files are committed; a variance note states the numeric range of p95 across those runs.
The hardware note names the machine or instance type and the number of warmup iterations discarded before the timed window.
